prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on who you’re traveling with and what you want to do.

Which to pick — quick guide
- Hotel — best if you want convenience, predictable service, easy access to shows/the Strip, daily housekeeping, on‑site restaurants/pools and front‑desk help. Good for short stays, couples who want downtown nightlife, or families who don’t want to clean or cook.
- Airbnb/cabin/VRBO — best if you want space, a kitchen, lake access, a porch/firepit, privacy, or you’re traveling with a group and want to lower cost per person. Great for longer stays, families or groups, and those who want a peaceful lakeside or wooded retreat.

Where to stay by travel style (specific, reliable options)

Luxury / couples / spa
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — high‑end lakeside resort, spa and nice views of Table Rock Lake.
- Big Cedar Lodge (nearby in Ridgedale) — upscale rustic resort with cabins, lodge rooms, golfing and outdoor amenities (a short drive from Branson’s shows).

Central / theater/“on the Strip” convenience
- Hampton Inn Branson on the Strip — reliable, close to shows and restaurants.
- Grand Country Inn (near the 76 Strip complex) — family‑friendly, attached to attractions.
- Hotels at Branson Landing / downtown — look for Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing or other Branson Landing hotels for walkability to shops and the waterfront.

Family / group-friendly hotels (pools, suites)
- Stoney Creek Hotel (or similar mid‑range Branson hotels with suites and indoor pools) — good for families.
- Many chain hotels along West 76 Country Boulevard offer suites and free breakfast (Hampton, Holiday Inn Express, Drury Inn, Best Western — check current availability).

Cabins & Airbnbs (best for space, lake access, groups)
- Table Rock Lake cabins or private homes around Branson West, Hollister, and Ridgedale — look for entire-cabin listings with multiple bedrooms, a full kitchen, dock/lake access, and strong Superhost/VRBO ratings.
- Condos or vacation homes near Silver Dollar City if that’s your focus (short drive).

Unique stays / local flavor
- The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — a distinctive, well‑rated property with good food and a quiet campus feel (book early).

How to pick the right specific property
- If you want easy access to shows/nightlife: book a hotel on/near the 76 Country Boulevard (the Strip) or Branson Landing.
- If you want outdoor recreation, privacy, or are a group: search for cabins/whole-home rentals on Table Rock Lake or near Silver Dollar City.
- Consider total cost: Airbnb/VRBO may look cheaper per night but add cleaning, service fees and sometimes parking; hotels add resort or parking fees.
- Check cancellation policies, parking availability, whether the property has AC (important in summer), and read recent reviews about cleanliness and host responsiveness.

If you tell me:
- travel dates (or season),
- group size and ages,
- budget per night,
- whether you want lakeside, near shows, or near Silver Dollar City —
I’ll give 5–8 specific current hotel and Airbnb listings (with pros/cons) that match your needs.
